clippings.speaker: Elia Kazan
clippings.quote: I just told him to get on his knees at the bottom of the staircase. But I didn't tell him what to do with his voice or how he should shout it. He just knew. But many, many things with him - many, many times with him, he was ahead of me…
clippings.title: Celebrating 30 Years Of 'Fresh Air': Filmmaker And Theater Legend Elia Kazan
clippings.context: Kazan to Terry Gross in 1988, when his autobiography came out, on directing the 'Stella' scene; rebroadcast 2017.

clippings.speaker: Elia Kazan
clippings.quote: He would've been damn good too, but not as good as Brando. I don't think anybody's as good as Brando.
clippings.title: Celebrating 30 Years Of 'Fresh Air': Filmmaker And Theater Legend Elia Kazan
clippings.context: Kazan on Frank Sinatra, first in line for Terry Malloy before the role went to Brando.

clippings.speaker: Elia Kazan
clippings.quote: Very, very little. I think we had a instinctive fraternity. I think we understood each other, almost from the word go, very well. And we would talk a lot about other things, but not a hell of a lot about the role.
clippings.title: Celebrating 30 Years Of 'Fresh Air': Filmmaker And Theater Legend Elia Kazan
clippings.context: Asked what questions Brando asked him about the Waterfront role.

clippings.speaker: Elia Kazan
clippings.quote: You adapt to what each one is. You - I talked more to Jimmy than I ever did to Marlon. … With Marlon, I didn't have to do anything like that.
clippings.title: Celebrating 30 Years Of 'Fresh Air': Filmmaker And Theater Legend Elia Kazan
clippings.context: Kazan comparing how he directed James Dean and Brando.

clippings.speaker: Marlon Brando
clippings.quote: Most actors don't get any help from directors. Emotional help, if you're playing an emotional part. Kazan is the only one I know who really gives you help.
clippings.title: Marlon Brando names the best director he ever worked with
clippings.context: From Chris Hodenfield's 1976 Rolling Stone interview, as quoted by Far Out Magazine in 2024.

clippings.speaker: Marlon Brando
clippings.quote: Kazan would say, 'Go out and rehearse this scene and bring me something back.' He'll take about eight points out of 12 or 11, and you argue with him. He'll give you points and there's no ego involved. He's a guy that works without ego.
clippings.title: Marlon Brando names the best director he ever worked with
clippings.context: Same 1976 Rolling Stone interview, as quoted by Far Out Magazine.

clippings.speaker: Marlon Brando
clippings.quote: Kazan was the best actors' director by far of any I've worked for . . . the only one who ever really stimulated me, got into a part with me and virtually acted it with me. . . . He was an arch-manipulator of actors' feelings, and he was extraordinarily talented; perhaps we will never see his like again.
clippings.title: 'On the Waterfront' and the Courage to Confront Evil
clippings.context: From Brando's 1994 autobiography, as quoted in a Word on Fire essay.

clippings.speaker: Marlon Brando
clippings.quote: They made the film to justify finking on their friends. Evidently, as Terry Malloy, I represented the spirit of the brave, courageous man who defied evil.
clippings.title: On the Waterfront (1954)
clippings.context: Brando's autobiography on Kazan and Schulberg's motives after Kazan named names to HUAC, as quoted by TCM.

notes: Kazan side is first-hand (1988 Fresh Air transcript); Brando side all secondhand (1976 Rolling Stone via Far Out, 1994 autobiography via Word on Fire/TCM). Variety 1999 piece on Brando declining to present Kazan's honorary Oscar was behind a tollbit redirect, skipped.
